content: Self-hosted webmail projects commonly fail at: (1) rendering email HTML without proper sandboxing — must use sandboxed iframe + DOMPurify + CSP; (2) IMAP UID as sole message identity — UIDs change on mailbox rebuild, must cross-reference with Message-ID; (3) SMTP port/encryption mismatch — port 465=implicit SSL, port 587=STARTTLS; shared hosting providers like GoDaddy hijack port 587; (4) attachment filename path traversal — CVE-2023-35169 in php-imap allowed RCE via unsanitized filenames; (5) storing mailbox passwords in plaintext; (6) Laravel shared hosting deployment — wrong document root, missing permissions, no APP_KEY; (7) IMAP connection exhaustion without pooling; (8) subject-only threading fails on real email; (9) setup wizard re-entrancy after installation; (10) CSS injection attacks bypassing HTML sanitization (Black Hat 2026).
